purpose: Table 3 task, Part A (user instruction, 29 Oct 2026): controlled-timing reruns of the Example 1 sensitivity runs results/nuts_Setting1_Ex1_sens_data96, _sens_data384, _sens_nkl24, _sens_nkl48 and _sens_nkl96 (19-20 Oct 2026, code, thread settings and machine load not recorded) with exactly their settings: NUTS, dense mass matrix, target 0.95, maximum tree depth 10, 500 warm-up iterations and 500 retained draws per chain, four chains, seeds 0-3, prior-draw starts, prior tau 16, alpha 4, k 14, mean a(2y - 1) with a = 2; data96 and data384 use the observation files of data meshes 96 and 384 with N_KL = 12, nkl24/48/96 the production observation file. Five batches, one after another, with nothing else heavy on the machine; load averages and the most CPU-intensive processes are recorded at the start and end of each batch. Each rerun is compared draw by draw with the earlier run. Declared and frozen before the runs; a change of any setting requires a new manifest id and output tag.

prior.n_kl_note: N_KL = 12 is the production value checked against config.py; the nkl stages override n_kl

model.plateau_bounds_note: joint-setting bounds of config.py, checked by the driver but not used by the v1 stages

data.note: existing observation files; their bytes are tracked in git and must not be regenerated. data_mesh_n = 192 refers to ex1; the ex1_mesh96 and ex1_mesh384 files use the same truth, electrodes and noise draw on data meshes 96 and 384

nuts.target_rationale: target 0.95, the setting of the earlier sensitivity runs being rerun

diagnostics.monitored: all KL coefficients and the junction depth at x = 0.5; c_p and c_n in the joint setting
diagnostics.undefined: an undefined R-hat or ESS of any monitored quantity means not passed
diagnostics.checkpoints: retrospective, on prefixes of the capped runs; costs from per-draw records; first pass reported with persistence, or 'not reached within the cap'

divergences.follow_up_rule: more than 0.5 % of the retained draws, or at least 3 divergences with 75 % or more in one chain
divergences.handling: report count, chain and location; keep the output; investigate the states; never change settings silently

timing.batches: one four-chain sampler batch at a time, no other heavy jobs on the machine
reported: aggregate worker time (sum over chains), sampling only and including warm-up
actual batch elapsed time from launch to the last chain end (epoch timestamps)
timing.excluded_from_sampler_timers: model construction and KL set-up (included in the batch elapsed time)

failure_handling: outputs are validated with check_run.py --production; an invalid output stops the driver and is kept for inspection; a valid run that fails the diagnostics or needs divergence follow-up is kept and flagged, never silently rerun with other settings
scope: Example 1, known plateaus (Setting 1): stages data96, data384, nkl24, nkl48, nkl96, run in this order, one four-chain batch at a time.

predeclared.reproduction: each rerun is compared draw by draw with the earlier run (all chains, all draws, step sizes, divergences, gradients per iteration); a difference is reported, not corrected
predeclared.reporting: for each batch: wall-clock time, minimum ESS per wall-clock second, worker time per PDE solve, Newton iterations per forward solve, load averages and processes at the start and end
predeclared.rules: the convergence thresholds and the divergence follow-up rule of production_v1 apply unchanged; no follow-up runs
predeclared.changes: no reruns, extensions or setting changes after seeing the results without the user's approval
